effect_estimate.comment: The ABM is deterministic so no confidence intervals or p-values are reported; quantitative outputs consist of benchmarked case-study WSD performance percentages and calibrated NetLogo payoff scores.
effect_estimate.value: Empirical WSD performance across the 5 benchmarked case studies was low: 20.0% to 26.6% (mean 23.3%) in Kenya (Old Town 20.0%, Migosi 26.6%, Kangemi 20.0%) and 13.3% to 20.0% (mean 16.6%) in Ghana (Madina 13.3%, Nima 20.0%). In the calibrated deterministic ABM (calibration parameter C = 1.6 in Kenya and 1.8 in Ghana, indicating social ties outweigh third-party participation; total system payoff = 61.0 to 67.0 in Kenya and 56.9 to 61.9 in Ghana for initial defection vs. initial cooperation), opportunistic management (low transparency, accountability, and participation [TAP] with power asymmetry) produces mutual-defection Prisoner's Dilemma strategies (Dd) and lower relative payoffs (+ to ++), whereas pragmatic management (low TAP with balanced power) produces Snow Drift strategies (Cd/Dc) and higher relative payoffs (++ to ++++).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 4, Section 'At the consumption level'; PDF p. 7, Table 5; PDF p. 9, Section 'Agent-based model (ABM) calibration'; PDF p. 11, Table 7; PDF p. 12, Section 'Overall Discussions and Conclusions'

mechanism_certainty.comment: Descriptive case-study scores document low TAP/governance integrity alongside low WSD performance across 5 urban utility areas (Table 5 and Table 7), while the behavioral principal-agent mechanism linking corruption risks and management practices to performance is simulated in a deterministic agent-based model rather than directly observed through primary fieldwork in this article. Per CODEBOOK.md §9, non-experimental designs cannot exceed 2, and 1 reflects documented descriptive association with simulated mechanistic dynamics.
